learningObjectives: Distinguish authentication from authorization in web applications.
Identify the main components of a Spring Security request flow.
Construct a basic protected API workflow using roles and authentication.

activities.title: Spring Security Request Flow
activities.instruction: Explore how a protected request is processed.

content.concept: Spring Security applies security processing to incoming requests. Authentication establishes the user's identity, while authorization determines whether that authenticated identity can access a protected resource.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: The HTTP request sent by a client.
A sequence of Spring Security filters that processes the request.
Verifies credentials or another identity mechanism and establishes an authenticated identity.
Checks whether the authenticated identity has permission to perform the requested operation.
The controller or endpoint that requires the configured security rules.

activities.title: Authentication vs Authorization
activities.instruction: Explore the distinction between identity and access.

content.concept: Authentication answers 'Who are you?' while authorization answers 'What are you allowed to access or do?' Both are important when protecting application resources.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Information such as a username and password used to establish identity.
The identity established after successful authentication.
A named group of permissions, such as USER or ADMIN.
A permission or granted access rule used during authorization.
A resource whose access is controlled by security rules.

activities.title: Access Rule Builder
activities.instruction: Build access rules for protected API endpoints.

content.concept: Spring Security rules can require authentication for an endpoint and can restrict access further using roles or authorities.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Security Decision
activities.instruction: Determine whether a request should be allowed.

content.concept: A request to a protected endpoint can proceed only when its authentication and authorization requirements are satisfied.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Authenticated USER requests an endpoint requiring USER
Unauthenticated client requests an endpoint requiring authentication
Authenticated USER requests an ADMIN-only endpoint
Authenticated client has no required authority
config.answer: Authenticated USER requests an endpoint requiring USER
